title: Policy assertion mapper, KMS region hardening, and audit watermarking
author: Maya Ortiz
description:
Summary: Add a policy-assertion mapper that converts incoming operator/service JWT claims into RBAC v2 directives, enforce KMS region pinning during the KMS handshake, and introduce a lightweight audit watermarking header for cross-region key-usage detection. Motivation: Recent compliance reviews and an internal incident (SUP-1193) showed ambiguous operator claims leading to accidental cross-region KMS calls and noisy audit streams that made investigating residency violations slow. This change tightens the policy -> RBAC mapping, rejects KMS requests incompatible with tenant region policies earlier, and tags audit events with a stable watermark for easier deduplication and correlation.

What this PR does (high level):
- policy/mapper: new PolicyAssertionMapper component that validates and normalizes JWT claims (operator.scope, tenant.region, service.zone) and emits RBAC v2 grant objects consumed by request-authorizer.
- kms/validator: KMS region pin checks during handshake and an opt-in strict-mode that returns a 412 (Precondition Failed) when a key operation is out-of-region for a tenant pinned by policy. Backwards-compatible default remains permissive with audit-only mode.
- audit/watermark: add X-Audit-Watermark (sha256 over request meta + timestamp bucket) to trace and dedupe cross-service audit lines, with config toggle and retention hints for downstream sink.
- rbac: small adjustments to rbac-v2 policy loader to accept mapped grant objects and to prefer explicit regional deny rules over generic allow rules.
- docs: security runbook and migration guide for operator teams to verify claims and enable strict KMS pinning.

Implementation notes:
- PolicyAssertionMapper lives under services/policy and is designed as a sidecar-friendly library so Dedicated/Private deployments can opt into translation without changing the control plane. It performs conservative normalization only (no claim augmentation).
- KMS region checks happen pre-encryption/decrypt attempt to fail fast and avoid potential cross-region telemetry leaks. There is a feature-flag (KMS_REGION_STRICT) that can be flipped per-tenant.
- Watermarking uses an HMAC-free SHA256 over canonicalized values (tenant_id, request_path, short-timestamp-bucket) so sinks can correlate without storing sensitive payloads. We intentionally avoid embedding key material in the watermark.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests for mapper normalization and rbac grant generation [x] Integration tests for KMS pre-checks in permissive and strict modes [x] End-to-end audit flow validation with watermark enabled [x] Documentation and migration guide [x] Feature flags and telemetry counters added

Testing and CI: Ran unit tests (services/policy/*), integration suite cover KMS region pinning scenarios, and an end-to-end smoke test that verifies watermark appears in all configured audit sinks. One flaky test in canary CI (integration/network) was retried and passed on rerun. Security scan (SNYK/Trivy) showed no new high/critical findings.

Rollout plan:
- Canary in us-west-2 with watermark and mapper enabled in audit-only mode for 48 hours.
- Enable KMS_REGION_STRICT for a small tenant cohort with customer opt-in and monitor errors for 7 days.
- Gradually expand strict mode after operator signoff; policy migration tooling included in docs to help tenants update claims.

Rollback: revert feature-flag or toggle mapper to audit-only mode. A small compatibility shim ensures older RBAC v1 checks will continue to operate until migration completes.

Related: ENG-4821 (policy mapping RFC), SEC-92 (compliance gap triage), SUP-1193 (incident follow-up).
